source: Adapted into original explanations and exercises from the supplied digitised Unit 2 and Unit 3 lecture notes. Unit 4 was a heading only and is not included.
scope: A first-year UK accounting companion, not an official University of Glasgow resource. Original exam-style questions rehearse the supplied topics; they are not past papers, predictions or an official marking scheme. Follow your lecturer's stated policies and assessment requirements. No VAT unless an exercise explicitly says otherwise; all amounts are GBP.
clarifications: Dividends paid to shareholders are distributions of equity, not an income statement expense. Interest on a loan is an expense. Drawings are owner withdrawals, not expenses.
LIFO is explained because it appears in the notes, but is not permitted under IAS 2 or FRS 102. Use FIFO or weighted average where applicable.

The loan notes' final entry describes a repayment, not receipt of a new loan. Equal allocation of total interest is used only when an exercise explicitly assumes it; real amortised-cost loans generally use the effective interest method.
A purchases account is used for goods bought for resale under the periodic inventory system in these introductory exercises. Buying equipment or paying rent does not go into purchases.

Grant income recognition depends on applicable standards and grant conditions. The grant exercises explicitly assume systematic release as the related costs arise. Receiving cash alone does not always create revenue.
